topic: xAI / SpaceXSI Grok Bot (always-on AI teammates) - research for a 60-second Instagram reel
notes_on_naming: x.ai pages call the company 'SpaceXSI' (footer: '(c) 2026 SpaceXAI LLC'); press calls it 'SpaceXAI'. xAI was acquired by SpaceX (x.ai/news/xai-joins-spacex, Feb 2 2026) and Cursor 'became part of SpaceXSI on August 14' 2026 (x.ai/news/grok-bot-customer-support). The App Store seller is 'X Corp.'; the app's description footer says (c) 2026 Anysphere, Inc. (Cursor's company).

claims.claim: Grok Bot launched in early beta on Aug 11, 2026. Official post: 'Introducing Grok Bot, now in early beta. Bots are AI teammates that do real work for you. They sign in to your tools, use them just like you do, and come back with finished work.' (@bot, Aug 11 2026 17:09 UTC, ~58M views). Blog headline: 'Today we're launching Grok Bot, AI teammates you can give real work to.'

sources.title: Introducing Grok Bot, now in early beta.

claims.claim: Musk on launch day: 'We will widen the Grok Bot beta after we fix basic issues with the early beta and release Grok 4.6 later this week'.

Bots run on a cloud computer that stays on: 'Bots share a computer of their own in the cloud, so jobs do not stall when you step away.' 'It's always on, with browser and terminal access. They sign into your apps and work happens in the actual tool instead of a chat draft.' Docs: 'Closing the Grok Bot app or your laptop does not stop cloud work.' Shared workspace at /workspace; computer screen is 1920x1200 (since v0.68.1).

claims.claim: Marketing says 'Bots have their own computer', but the docs say all of a user's Bots share ONE cloud computer: browser cookies and sign-ins, files and command-line credentials are shared, and 'do not use separate Bots as a security boundary'. Each Bot has its own screen and can run one computer-use task at a time.

claims.claim: Difference from normal Grok chat: Grok Bot is a separate app (desktop + iOS) where named, persistent Bots work in your real tools, remember how you work, run in parallel, coordinate in group chats, and keep working after you leave. 'Other AI tools may ask you to set up and build workflows and routines first. With Grok Bot, simply message a Bot to take on a task and it gets it done.' App Store: 'takes projects from start to finish instead of leaving you with another chat draft.'

'A chief of staff sits on top, with a specialist for each lane: inbox management, expenses, recruiting, bug fixes, or operations.' Bots 'can independently message each other and share context in threads' and coordinate in group chats.

Show a Bot a workflow once and it saves it as a routine that runs on its own. Docs: 'A Bot can own up to 50 routines'; 'Routine schedules must be at least five minutes apart'; teaching records up to ten minutes of screen activity; routines can also be triggered by events (Slack, GitHub, Microsoft Teams, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty, webhooks).

claims.claim: Official use-case gallery includes marketing/business bots: Competitive Intelligence Analyst ('Monitors overnight for new launches and audits your site for fatigued creatives and stale messaging'), LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Newsletter Writer, SEO / AEO Auditor, Paid Media ('holds for your approval before making adjustments'), Event Guest Screener, Sales Outbound ('Researches accounts overnight... drafts email and LinkedIn in your voice'), Inbox Manager ('Every send stays behind your approval'), Chief of Staff, Travel Coordinator, Apartment Scout, Subscription Cleaner, Hiring Screener, Talent Scout.

xAI's internal procurement Bot 'Haggle Bot' 'has identified more than $100,000 in direct savings'; found 43 paid seats unused for 90 days ($14,220) and $85,662/yr in unused SKUs on another product. Required approval for spending, accepting terms or contacting vendors. (Company self-report.)

claims.claim: Platforms: macOS (Apple silicon & Intel), Windows (x64 & Arm64), Linux (x64 & Arm64), iOS 18+ via App Store. Setup: install desktop app, sign in, first Bot is created automatically, give it a job, sign in to tools via 'Open computer'/Take over (you type passwords/2FA yourself), review and save routines, read approvals guidance. Android not listed.

418,000 WEEKLY users as of Sept 14, 2026, up 24% week on week, per a company presentation seen by Bloomberg (reported Sept 22). Not published by xAI itself; no newer number found. Treat as 'reported by Bloomberg', not official.

claims.claim: @bot account has ~422,000 followers (Oct 19, 2026). Launch video post ~58M views. App Store US rating 4.9 from ~11,900 ratings. No official count of Bots created. Limits: up to 50 routines per Bot; schedules >= 5 min apart; teach-by-demo up to 10 min; approvals from unattended runs expire after ~10 minutes; usage is a weekly pool.

Docs advise explicit boundaries for sending, publishing, purchases, deleting, permission changes, production changes and accepting legal terms; approval cards offer allow once / always allow / deny; optional Auto-review; use 'Take over' for passwords, 2FA, CAPTCHAs and payments ('Never send passwords or one-time codes in ordinary chat'); local-computer access defaults to 'Ask every time'; start with read-only tasks.
